incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — financial crime (Tren de Aragua)
incidents.vector: Malware installed on ATM hardware forces machines to dispense cash on command; proceeds laundered through cryptocurrency networks.
incidents.impact: More than $40.7 million stolen across 1,500+ ATM jackpotting attacks in the U.S. OFAC sanctioned 10 members of the network today; 98 individuals have been indicted federally. Fugitive engineer known as 'Prometheus' remains at large as the FBI's most-wanted cybercriminal.

incidents.victim: NGOs, Think Tanks, and Governments (100+ organizations, primarily U.S. and U.K.)
incidents.vector: Large-scale phishing campaigns use password-protected archives containing LNK files that trigger the RedFlick infection chain; the technique replaced ClickFix as FSB's preferred initial-access lure in 2026.
incidents.impact: CosmicPulse Python backdoor deployed across 100+ organizations since January 2026, with 13 distinct large-scale campaigns identified. Targets include Ukrainian institutions, NGOs supporting Ukraine, and Western policy organizations in the U.S. and U.K.

incidents.victim: Specific High-Value Individuals (iOS users on versions before iOS 27)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — likely nation-state or commercial spyware operator
incidents.vector: An out-of-bounds write in Apple's CoreGraphics framework (CVE-2026-86950, CVSS 8.8) allows arbitrary code execution; Apple describes the attack as 'extremely sophisticated' and targeted against specific individuals on iOS before version 27.
incidents.impact: Apple issued emergency patches for iOS 26, macOS Tahoe, and macOS Sequoia. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog with a mandatory remediation deadline for federal agencies. Scope of compromise among targeted individuals has not been publicly disclosed. Meta Product Security team credited with discovery.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited an undisclosed vulnerability in Dodo Pizza's customer management platform to extract customer records at scale.
incidents.impact: Attackers claimed 68 million customer records across 28 countries, including names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, and order histories. Dodo Pizza confirmed unauthorized access to some customer data; no payment card information reportedly compromised. Investigation ongoing across 1,500 global locations.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised one of three hot wallet layers at Singapore-based crypto exchange Bitget, draining operational liquidity reserves used for customer transactions.
incidents.impact: $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen from Bitget's hot wallets — the largest crypto heist of 2026. The exchange confirmed the breach and the source of the stolen funds; no further attribution has been established.

incidents.vector: A suspected autonomous AI agent breached DIVD's internal systems through an undisclosed attack path; full technical details are pending the organization's own post-incident analysis.
incidents.impact: Internal systems of the Dutch non-profit, which coordinates responsible vulnerability disclosures to software vendors, were compromised. DIVD is investigating and has pledged to publish a full post-mortem.

incidents.victim: Government, Financial Services, Education, Telecom, and Legal Sectors (North America and Europe)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — advanced and suspected state-sponsored threat actors
incidents.vector: Two critical zero-days in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway exploited against default configurations: CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated RCE via input validation flaw, CVSS 9.5) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow RCE/DoS, CVSS 9.5).
incidents.impact: Mandiant confirms dozens of organizations compromised across North America and Europe; earliest exploitation observed September 3 — more than three weeks before Citrix's public disclosure on September 27. More than 50,000 exposed instances identified globally. UK NCSC and CISA both issued emergency alerts.

incidents.vector: Exploited CVE-2026-35273, a critical vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft, to breach the FBI's job application portal; bypassed Mandiant's published WAF workaround using URL-encoding tricks.
incidents.impact: Social Security numbers and personal records of 5,000+ FBI officials stolen, including medical history, psychiatric records, job assignments, unit details, and family member information — creating direct counterintelligence and physical safety risks. The FBI confirmed the breach and defaced their site. Dutch police arrested a suspected ShinyHunters member; ShinyHunters also mass-exploited PeopleSoft against dozens of other organizations in higher education, healthcare, technology, and government sectors.

incidents.victim: ATNS (Air Traffic and Navigation Services), South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware-linked malware was deployed in OT networks supporting weather and air traffic services at Port Elizabeth and East London airports; data exfiltration to IP addresses located in China was observed.
incidents.impact: ATNS manages approximately 10% of the world's airspace. Technical teams implemented containment measures; a formal digital forensic investigation has been requested. A related incident at Maputo International Airport in Mozambique is also under investigation for possible insider-assisted data theft.

incidents.vector: Initial access via self-service password reset; attacker registered their own MFA device, then used legitimate Azure DevOps pipelines and automated scripts to enumerate repositories and harvest Kubernetes credentials at scale.
incidents.impact: Kubeconfig files for 50+ Kubernetes resources obtained; persistent access established via Atera RMM and Chisel tunneling tools. Microsoft DART responded and evicted the threat actor after detecting anomalous pipeline behavior.

incidents.victim: Medyc and MyDr (Polish Healthcare Software Platforms)
incidents.vector: Medyc breached in late August via SQL injection in its application interface; MyDr compromised through an undisclosed vulnerability. The same hacker group is suspected in both attacks based on technical indicators.
incidents.impact: MyDr breach exposed records on approximately 19 million patients across 12,000 healthcare organizations. Medyc attackers claimed 5 million patient records and 8 million private medical photographs, including psychiatric and addiction treatment files. Both platforms serve Poland's national healthcare system.

incidents.victim: Organizations Using Zimbra Collaboration Suite (Multiple Sectors, Multiple Regions)
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated OS command injection via CVE-2026-73570 in Zimbra's SNMP notification path; attackers sent crafted SMTP requests triggering execution as the Zimbra service account before patch availability.
incidents.impact: JSP webshells deployed and privilege escalation achieved via Zimbra's PAM configuration; email content, LDAP credentials, pre-auth keys, and token material exfiltrated. Exploitation activity began July 28 — more than two weeks before public disclosure on August 13. Multiple sectors and geographic regions affected.

incidents.vector: ClickFix social engineering via a fake video conferencing website: victim was presented with a fabricated meeting error and instructed to run a PowerShell and VBScript infection chain.
incidents.impact: Two previously unknown malware families deployed on the victim's endpoint: GeniexLoader (staged dropper) and GeniexRAT (remote access tool), enabling persistent access and potential data theft from the financial services target.

incidents.victim: Government, Defense, Foreign Affairs, and Legislative Organizations (Taiwan, India, Philippines, Cambodia, Pakistan, Thailand, Myanmar, Syria)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing emails with cloned Gmail attachment widgets delivered a five-stage infection chain via Cloudflare infrastructure; final payload is the Antino Rust-compiled backdoor, which uses Microsoft 365 Outlook and OneDrive as command-and-control channels to blend with legitimate cloud traffic.
incidents.impact: Approximately 350 endpoints compromised across eight Asian countries, spanning defense ministries, executive government, foreign affairs offices, parliamentary institutions, and law enforcement agencies. Campaign active from September 2025 through July 2026.

incidents.vector: Compromised Azure service principal credentials — previously leaked in a public GitHub issue's edit history — used to conduct a 15-hour automated reconnaissance of the entire Azure environment, followed by rapid deletion of storage accounts, Key Vault, and application resources.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of Azure storage accounts deleted along with Key Vault, Function App, and App Service plan — consistent with a ransomware or extortion operation, though no ransom note was confirmed. Microsoft has observed this threat actor probing multiple Azure environments across the year.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian-Affiliated Employees at Organizations in France, U.S., and Canada
incidents.vector: Compromised Ukrainian websites served fake CAPTCHA pages to Ukrainian visitors; users were tricked into executing PowerShell commands that downloaded and ran VBScript payloads, providing persistent access to targeted workstations.
incidents.impact: Multiple organizations employing Ukrainian staff were compromised via the ClickFix technique across France, the U.S., and Canada. CrowdStrike Falcon Complete MDR detected and contained the intrusions; ongoing campaign consistent with GRU intelligence collection targeting Ukrainian diaspora.

incidents.vector: Fraudsters used AI-cloned voice synthesis to impersonate a lawyer in calls to Fideuram's chairman, presenting fabricated authorization from Intesa Sanpaolo's CEO to approve large wire transfers to Chinese and Hong Kong bank accounts.
incidents.impact: €95 million ($108M) fraudulently transferred from Italy's largest bank's private banking arm. Intesa Sanpaolo recovered more than half the funds; €36 million remains missing. The incident is one of the largest confirmed AI-enabled financial fraud cases to date.

incidents.vector: Social engineering: a Dutch-speaking ShinyHunters member telephoned an Odido employee, impersonated an internal colleague, and directed the victim to authenticate at a spoofed Odido portal, harvesting credentials used to extract customer records.
incidents.impact: Data on 6.2 million Dutch people stolen — a large fraction of the Netherlands' population — including personal and account information. Dutch police subsequently arrested a suspected ShinyHunters member in the Netherlands in connection with this and related breaches.

incidents.victim: Telecommunications, Universities, Intergovernmental Organizations, Government Contractors
incidents.vector: Post-compromise deployment of NeedyMantis, a modular backdoor using DLL sideloading alongside legitimate software (Poedit, curl, TightVNC) to evade detection; communicates via WebSockets with a custom-encrypted archive format and uses a Set-Cookie header to exfiltrate host metadata on first contact.
incidents.impact: Long-term persistent access established across targeted organizations beginning October 2025; linked by Microsoft to the prior DAEMON Tools supply chain compromise. Modular architecture allows selective capability loading — only the capabilities needed for a specific target are deployed, reducing detection surface.

incidents.vector: A misconfigured file-sharing system left military personnel data publicly accessible without authentication for approximately nine months.
incidents.impact: Unauthorized parties accessed names, military information, and Social Security numbers of DMDC members between October 2025 and July 2026. The Pentagon confirmed unauthorized access occurred during the exposure window; scope of downstream exploitation is not publicly known.
